newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRANCE RECOVER TO BEAT DUTCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRANCE RECOVER TO BEAT DUTCH.

text.p: Home-based substitutes Patrice Loko and Robert Pires scored in the last 16 minutes to give 1998 World Cup hosts France a 2-1 win over the Netherlands in an international friendly on Wednesday.

Arsenal striker Dennis Bergkamp, running on to a fine through ball from Ajax Amsterdam's Ronald de Boer, had put the Dutch ahead in the third minute when he rifled a 25-metre shot past Bernard Lama in the French goal.

But Pires equalised in the 74th when he curled in a shot from the left and 10 minutes later Paris St Germain striker Loko hit the winner after a good run down the right by Christophe Dugarry of AC Milan.

Bergkamp could have put the match beyond French reach in the first-half when he broke away again, but after Lama forced him wide his late shot was blocked on the line by France's stand-in captain Laurent Blanc.

The Dutch had been unbeaten since falling 4-1 to England in the European championship in June, but had lost to France on penalties in the Euro 96 quarter-finals after a 0-0 draw and had also lost their previous meeting with the French since coach Aime Jacquet took charge.

"We were not attentive enough at the start and that's something we've learnt from this match. (In the second half) France recovered their elan, their strength and dynamism," said Jacquet, who made a telling substitution after half an hour by bringing on Metz winger Pires for midfielder Pierre Laigle, one of nine foreign-based players in the starting line-up, to stretch the Dutch defence.
France hardly troubled Dutch keeper Edwin van der Sar in the first half which the visitors dominated, employing the style that has produced 13 goals in three World Cup qualifiers.
But the French took charge after the interval, coming close on several occasions, not least a downward header by Christian Karembeu that Seedorf blocked on the line.

Dutch stand-in coach Jan Rab said: "We had a very good first half, when we kept possession well. The second was totally different. Our players were too individual and we gave away corners which were very dangerous."

France - 1-Bernard Lama; 15-Lilian Thuram, 5-Laurent Blanc, 8-Marcel Desailly, 3-Bixente Lizarazu (14-Vincent Candela 87); 13-Ibrahim Ba (9-Patrice Loko 78), 19-Christian Karembeu, 12-Pierre Laigle (7-Robert Pires 32), 6-Patrick Vieira (4-Bruno N'Gotty 78), 10-Zinedine Zidane; 11-Christophe Dugarry.

Netherlands - 1-Edwin van der Sar; 2-Michael Reiziger, 3-Japp Stam, 4-Frank de Boer, 5-Arthur Numan; 6-Wim Jonk, 7-Ronald de Boer, 10-Clarence Seedorf (12-Marc Overmars 72), 11-Philip Cocu (14-Giovanni van Bronckhorst 78); 8-Dennis Bergkamp, 9-Patrick Kluivert.
